headline: AI companies and Australia's music industry are arguing before a parliamentary committee over whether copyright law should allow AI training without permission.
score_reason: Pool 5 lowered by 1: the hearing was on 6 Oct 2026, before the window, and the MLex text could not be read.
importance_line: Writers, musicians and broadcasters could see their work used to train AI without payment if Australia relaxes its rules, while AI companies say licensing every work is unworkable, but nothing has been decided and the committee reports by 30 Nov 2026.
summary: MLex reports that OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Microsoft have flagged Australian copyright barriers to training AI; Law Commentary's account of a parliamentary hearing on 6 Oct 2026 adds that Anthropic's representative Jeffrey Bleich said licensing each work used in training is technically impossible, while the recording-industry body ARIA warned against making Australia a "Trojan horse for Big AI". The government ruled out a broad exception for AI training in October 2025 and prefers voluntary licensing; our 6 Oct 2026 edition covered other parts of that hearing.
notes: Desk-built entry: MLex is paywalled (headline only, so the Google and Microsoft part rests on that headline alone); facts read at Law Commentary, which reports the 6 Oct 2026 hearing of the Joint Select Committee on AI. Law Commentary names OpenAI and Anthropic but not Google or Microsoft. Stale: event before 8 Oct 2026. Follow-up of our 6 Oct 2026 edition (Forbes Australia item on Anthropic and the AI Safety Institute).
